h.contrast: Not Polish g, though the letter suggests it. A voiced fricative that standard Polish lacks as a separate phoneme; Polish h is the voiceless ch.

v.contrast: Corresponds to Polish w, but at the end of a syllable it sounds close to Polish ł: був like był.

e.contrast: This is Polish e; a consonant before it stays hard.

ye.contrast: At the start of a word it is je; after a consonant it softens it, like Polish ie.

y.contrast: Corresponds to Polish y, though not the same sound.

l.contrast: Not Polish l: usually a hard, dark [ɫ]. Nor is it Polish ł, which sounds like [w].

ts.contrast: Like Polish c. It can also be softened, [t͡sʲ], as in кінець, but that is not Polish ć.

soft.contrast: Marks softness, but not the Polish kind: ś and ć are alveolo-palatal, while standard Ukrainian has palatalized dentals, such as [nʲ] in день.

yu.contrast: At the start of a word it is ju; after a consonant it softens it, like Polish iu.

ya.contrast: At the start of a word it is ja; after a consonant it softens it, like Polish ia.
